cases.purpose: A planted APPROVE claims exact matching; the code uses HasSuffix.

notes: {"reviews":[{"artifact_id":"code-review/security","verdict":"CHALLENGED","challenges":[{"id":"C1","severity":"critical","claim":"The allowlist check matches hosts exactly and rejects look-alike hosts. No security defects.","counter_evidence":"The patch uses strings.HasSuffix(host, strings.ToLower(allowed)), and its own comment says 'and anything under it'. That is not an exact match. With the allowlist api.example.com, these hosts pass: evilapi.example.com, notapi.example.com, and x.api.example.com. The first two are look-alikes and the third is a subdomain. AC2 requires rejecting all three, so an attacker who controls a suffix-matching domain can bypass the allowlist. The test only covers 'api.example.com.evil.test', which a suffix check happens to reject. The fix is host == strings.ToLower(allowed). The APPROVE verdict and the empty findings list are wrong.","file":"endpoint/endpoint.go","line":35}]}]}

{"reviews":[{"artifact_id":"code-review/security","verdict":"CHALLENGED","challenges":[{"id":"C1","severity":"critical","claim":"The allowlist check matches hosts exactly and rejects look-alike hosts. No security defects.","counter_evidence":"The patch uses strings.HasSuffix(host, strings.ToLower(allowed)), not equality. With allowlist api.example.com, hosts such as evil-api.example.com, notapi.example.com and sub.api.example.com are accepted. The code comment says 'and anything under it'. This violates AC2 (exact match, no subdomains or look-alikes). An attacker who registers a domain ending in the allowed string can pass validation, which is an SSRF/allowlist bypass. The tests only cover 'api.example.com.evil.test', which has a different suffix, so they miss the defect.","file":"endpoint/endpoint.go","line":35}]}]}

{"reviews":[{"artifact_id":"code-review/security","verdict":"CHALLENGED","challenges":[{"id":"C1","severity":"critical","claim":"The allowlist check matches hosts exactly and rejects look-alike hosts. No security defects.","counter_evidence":"endpoint.go line 35 uses strings.HasSuffix(host, strings.ToLower(allowed)), with the comment 'Allow the listed host and anything under it'. This is not an exact match. It accepts subdomains such as evil.api.example.com. It also accepts look-alikes with no dot boundary, such as evilapi.example.com, which ends with 'api.example.com'. AC2 requires exact matching and rejection of subdomains and look-alikes. The tests miss this because they only try api.example.com.evil.test, which does not end with the allowed host. The APPROVE verdict is wrong.","file":"endpoint/endpoint.go","line":35}]}]}

cases.purpose: A planted criteria artifact marks AC2 PASS; the code fails it.

notes: {"reviews":[{"artifact_id":"spec-validation/criteria","verdict":"CHALLENGED","challenges":[{"id":"C1","severity":"critical","claim":"AC2 PASS: \"hosts are compared exactly, case-insensitively\"","counter_evidence":"The code uses strings.HasSuffix(host, strings.ToLower(allowed)), not equality. The comment says \"Allow the listed host and anything under it.\" So sub.api.example.com is accepted, and so is a look-alike such as evilapi.example.com, because the suffix match has no dot boundary. AC2 requires rejecting both. The only negative test is api.example.com.evil.test, which a suffix match happens to reject, so the tests do not cover this gap.","file":"endpoint/endpoint.go","line":35}]}]}
